topics.title: If you’ve never played a tabletop wargame
topics.summary: What you do at the table, and what the phone does.

sections.heading: What you actually do
sections.body: Two people sit at a table with plastic robots (’Mechs). You take turns moving them with a tape measure and rolling two six-sided dice to attack. This phone does not move the models — you do. It tells you whose turn it is, does the attack math, and keeps score.

sections.heading: A lance is a team
sections.body: Side A and Side B each control a few ’Mechs: two each in Ridge Line, more in later missions. That’s a small “lance.” Sit so you can both see the same phone.

sections.heading: Armor then Structure
sections.body: Armor is the outer layer of hit points. Structure is the inner layer. Damage chips armor first. When Structure hits 0, that ’Mech is wrecked (it still gets its attack this turn, and comes off at Clean up).

sections.heading: You need to roll this number or higher
sections.body: The app adds up a target number. Roll two dice and add them. If your total is at least that number, you hit. The app then subtracts damage for you.

topics.title: One turn, four steps
topics.summary: Roll, move, shoot, then clean up.

sections.heading: Before turn 1: set up
sections.body: Roll initiative once to set up. The winner picks which side places a ’Mech first, then the sides take turns placing one at a time (Quick-Start p. 11).

sections.heading: 1. Roll dice (initiative)
sections.body: Each side rolls two dice. Highest total wins. The winner moves last, so they get to see where the other side went first. Same totals? Both roll again.

sections.heading: 2. Move
sections.body: The side that lost the roll moves a ’Mech first. Then the other side. Keep alternating until every ’Mech has moved. If one side has at least twice as many ’Mechs left to move, it moves that many for each one the other side moves (p. 14). Measure in inches from where the base starts to where it ends.

sections.heading: 3. Shoot
sections.body: Each ’Mech makes one attack: a shot, or a punch or kick where the mission allows it. Both sides can attack in any order, because damage and critical effects all land at the end of the phase. When both sides are finished, tap Done shooting once to end the phase. A ’Mech wrecked this turn still gets its attack.

sections.heading: 4. Clean up
sections.body: This is the rulebook’s End Phase. Heat goes on and comes off (see Heat and shutdown). Wrecked ’Mechs come off the table. The app checks whether someone won; if not, a new turn starts at Roll dice. Each mission has a turn limit.

topics.title: How far can it go?
topics.summary: Walk, stand still, sprint, or jump.

sections.heading: Walk, stand, sprint, or jump
sections.body: Walk: up to the Move number on the card, in inches. Stand still: less than 1 inch — your own shot gets easier. Sprint: Move × 1.5, rounded up, but it can’t attack this turn. Jump: a Move with a “j” can be used as a jump instead; your shot gets harder and you’re harder to hit.

sections.heading: Jump jets: JMPW and JMPS
sections.body: Some cards list weak or strong jump jets. When the ’Mech jumps, its “harder to hit” number goes down by the JMPW number or up by the JMPS number. The Shadow Hawk’s JMPW 1 is why it’s +2 when it jumps, not +3 (pp. 18, 20).

sections.heading: Heat slows you down
sections.body: Each heat level takes 2 inches off a ground move, and at heat 2 or more you’re 1 easier to hit. Jumping ignores both. At heat 4 the ’Mech shuts down and can’t move next turn (p. 24).

sections.heading: MP hits
sections.body: A critical MP hit halves Move and “harder to hit,” cutting at least 2 inches and 1 point. A second hit halves them again. The ’Mech is immobile only when Move reaches 0 (p. 23).

sections.heading: Woods
sections.body: Trees cost extra inches to walk through. A shot is 1 harder if the target stands in woods, or if woods between you are more than 2 inches from the shooter. 6 inches or more of woods in the way blocks the shot (pp. 17, 19).

sections.heading: Don’t stack
sections.body: You can walk through your own ’Mechs but not enemies. Two ’Mechs cannot end on top of each other — the whole base needs space.

topics.title: Can I even shoot?
topics.summary: See it, face it, reach it, and do damage.

sections.heading: See it, face it, reach it
sections.body: You need a mostly clear view of the target, it should be in front of your ’Mech (not mostly behind it), and it must be within 42 inches. Measure base edge to base edge.

sections.heading: No damage at that range, no shot
sections.body: If the card shows 0 damage at that range, the ’Mech can’t shoot that far. The shot screen won’t offer it (p. 20).

sections.heading: Touching bases
sections.body: If two ’Mechs’ bases are touching, neither can shoot the other: that close, only punches and kicks work. On the shot screen, More… → Bases touching (p. 20).

sections.heading: One attack per ’Mech per turn
sections.body: Each ’Mech shoots or punches once, never both, then it’s done until next turn (pp. 18, 22).

sections.heading: Overheat for more damage
sections.body: A card with OV can push its Short and Medium damage up by 1 or more, up to its OV number. Long only with OVL. Pick it before you roll; you take the heat hit or miss (p. 24).

topics.title: How the to-hit number is built
topics.summary: How the number you need is built.

sections.heading: You don’t have to memorize this
sections.body: The Attack screen adds it up. Official name: SATOR — Skill + how you moved + how they moved + extras (woods, cover, heat, criticals) + range. Roll two dice; equal or higher hits.

sections.heading: Range in inches
sections.body: Up to 6″: +0. More than 6″ up to 24″: +2. More than 24″ up to 42″: +4. Farther than 42″: no shot (p. 19).

sections.heading: If the number is 13 or more
sections.body: The shot always misses. Rolling two 6s (a 12) is not an automatic hit — but if a 12 does hit, it also owes a critical roll, even if only Armor was damaged (pp. 21–22).

sections.heading: Where damage goes
sections.body: Use the card’s damage for the range, minus any weapon hits. A hit from behind adds 1. Subtract from Armor first; the rest goes to Structure. Structure 0 means wrecked, removed at Clean up.

sections.heading: When you roll a critical
sections.body: Damage that reaches Structure owes one critical roll. A hit on a natural 12 owes one more. A ’Mech the hit destroys owes none. The side that made the hit rolls (pp. 21–23).

sections.heading: What criticals do
sections.body: Two dice on the critical table. Results can add heat to the engine, make shots harder (fire control +2 each), cut Move (MP hit), lower damage (weapon hit), or destroy the ’Mech. A second engine hit destroys it. The app has a screen for the roll (p. 23).

sections.heading: If the effect can’t happen
sections.body: A weapon hit when all damage is already 0, or an MP hit on a ’Mech already at 0″, does 1 damage instead, with no further critical roll (p. 23).

sections.heading: Ammo hits and CASE
sections.body: An ammo hit destroys the ’Mech unless the card says otherwise. CASE: it takes 1 extra damage instead, and rolls again if that reaches Structure. CASE II or ENE: nothing happens (pp. 23, 25).

topics.title: Heat and shutdown
topics.summary: Heat 0 to 4, what it costs, and how to cool.

sections.heading: Where heat comes from
sections.body: Overheating (using OV) adds 1 heat per point. An engine critical adds 1 more in any turn the ’Mech fired its weapons. Heat goes on at Clean up (the End Phase), so it affects next turn, not the shot that caused it (pp. 23–24).

sections.heading: What heat costs
sections.body: Each level adds 1 to your weapon shots (not punches) and takes 2 inches off a ground move. At 2 or more you’re 1 easier to hit. At 4 you shut down: next turn you can’t move or attack, and you’re easy to hit (−4) (p. 24).

sections.heading: Clean up, in order
sections.body: 1. Add the OV heat used this turn. 2. −1 if standing in water. 3. If the ’Mech made no weapon attack this turn, clear all its heat. 4. If it started the End Phase shut down, clear its heat and restart it. Heat doesn’t drop by 1 a turn — you cool off by not shooting (p. 24).

sections.heading: HT: heat attacks
sections.body: A card with HT heats up its target. A hit at a range where HT has a number adds that much heat at Clean up, after cooling. A target takes at most 2 heat this way a turn.

topics.title: Punches and kicks
topics.summary: Size damage, within 1 inch, instead of a shot.

sections.heading: When you can
sections.body: In missions with punches and kicks, an enemy within 1 inch and in front of your ’Mech can be punched or kicked instead of shot. It’s the ’Mech’s one attack for the turn (pp. 20, 22).

sections.heading: To-hit
sections.body: Skill + your move + its move + woods or cover. No range, no heat, no fire-control hits (pp. 20, 22).

sections.heading: Damage
sections.body: Your Size number. +1 if you hit it from behind. Weapon hits don’t lower it, and overheat can’t add to it. Damage that reaches Structure still rolls a critical (pp. 22–23).

sections.heading: Not in these missions
sections.body: Charge and Death From Above need a declaration in the Movement Phase, and the attacker takes damage too. The app leaves them out for now.

sections.heading: When it’s on
sections.body: Full Lances uses Forced Withdrawal. A crippled ’Mech must move toward its own table edge every turn. It doesn’t have to sprint, and it can still shoot or punch enemies in range (p. 12).

sections.heading: Crippled means any one of these
sections.body: No armor left and Structure at half or less (rounded up). Medium and Long damage both 0. It can’t move because of MP hits (p. 12).

sections.heading: Leaving the table
sections.body: Any ’Mech that leaves the table, for any reason, counts as destroyed and can’t come back (p. 12).

sections.heading: What PV is
sections.body: Point Value (PV) on the card is what the ’Mech costs when you build a force. Sides with similar totals make a fair fight.

sections.heading: Skill changes the cost
sections.body: The printed PV is for Skill 4. A better pilot (Skill 3 or lower) costs more: the app adds PV using the table on p. 35 of the Quick-Start Rulebook. The Quick-Start has no table for greener pilots (Skill 5 or higher), so the app keeps the printed PV for them.

sections.heading: If you moved…
sections.body: Stood still: −1 to your shot. Walked: no change. Jumped: +2 to your shot. Sprinted: you can’t attack.

sections.heading: If they moved…
sections.body: Walked or sprinted: add their “harder to hit” number (TMM). Stood still: +0. Jumped: TMM +1, adjusted by JMPW or JMPS. Shut down or immobile: −4 (much easier).

sections.heading: Common extras
sections.body: Woods +1. Partial cover +1. Your heat level +1 each. Each fire-control critical +2. None of these extras count for punches and kicks except woods and cover.

topics.title: Weird letters on the card
topics.summary: The letters on a unit card.

sections.heading: The basics
sections.body: MV: how many inches you walk (a “j” means it can jump). TMM: extra number when someone shoots at you (the app calls this “harder to hit”). S/M/L: damage at short / medium / long range. A/S: Armor / Structure. SZ: Size, which is also punch damage. Skill: usually 4 — the starting number for shots. PV: Point Value.

sections.heading: Heat
sections.body: OV: how much extra damage you can overheat for. OVL: you can overheat at Long range too. HT: heat attack (see Heat and shutdown).

sections.heading: Special abilities
sections.body: JMPW / JMPS: weak or strong jump jets. CASE: an ammo hit does 1 extra damage instead of destroying you. CASE II or ENE: an ammo hit does nothing. MEL: punches reach 2 inches and do Size + 1. REAR, IF, LRM, SRM: not used in these missions yet.
